target: Route "one-player-howard": Howard with two actions — a superlinear all-switches family of one-player stopping SSGs, or a polynomial bound

findings.defect: Unattributed rediscovery of the paper's own sec:readouts. oph:dictionary is exactly lem:readout(a,b,c) specialised to Vmin = empty (where lem:readout(a) already says the readout is 'a single substochastic affine map') plus thm:readout-realise(b) at r = 1, which already gives 'exactly m Max vertices, 0 Min vertices, at most 2m(m+1)D average vertices' — the route's own O(m^2 d). The first-passage collapse it proves as its key display, val_rho(v) = sum_{w in C} p^{v,rho(v)}_w val_rho(w) + q, is verbatim the display inside the proof of lem:rise-bound (l.4111-4114), which itself calls it 'the collapse of the average part that also underlies thm:impedance'. The MDP reading it announces is already asserted in prose at rem:ladder ('the open question they leave -- whether Howard's rule is superpolynomial with two actions per state -- is precisely the one-player half of the pivot'), at rem:grid-per-vertex, at rem:four-ceilings and at rem:lasserre ('transient two-action Markov decision processes'). So (v3) was settled by round 15's own sec:readouts and nobody noticed; the route re-proves it from scratch citing none of lem:readout, lem:readout-reduce, thm:readout-realise or lem:rise-bound. rem:oph:v3's added clarification ('N is the encoding length O(m^2 d), not the number of states') is rem:four-ceilings' 'whether h*_1 grows superpolynomially, and is attained on m^{O(1)} vertices'.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.6707-6746 (def:readout-system, thm:readout-realise), l.6644-6656 (lem:readout(a): 'a single substochastic affine map when Vmin = emptyset'), l.6658-6668 (lem:readout(b),(c)), l.4110-4115 (lem:rise-bound's proof display), l.7143-7147 (rem:ladder), l.7228-7232 (rem:grid-per-vertex), l.12345 (rem:lasserre).

findings.defect: Presented as a new polynomial class ('SSG-Value restricted to the sign-definite games is in P') with NO member exhibited outside the eight known classes. The bar in this paper is prop:modulator-family and prop:fv-family, both of which check every structural parameter of an explicit family against every other class on the reachable subgame. The route's evidence is 882 + 1009 random stopping SSGs with n in 8..13, |Vmax| in 2..4 and |Vmin| in 0..2 — every single one of which has min(m,k) <= 2 = O(log N) and is therefore in the trivial class, so the sample cannot separate anything and does not vary the parameter the class turns on. It also reports no control group (no measurement of non-sign-definite games at the same sizes), so 'longest run inside the class is 3' carries no information: random games of that size have short runs anyway. Separately, the m = 1 special case of the theorem (a Max vertex whose other option is a constant switches at most twice) is stated twice in the paper's own prose, both times citing lem:switch, and is not cited.
findings.evidence: t_signdef.py lines 'n = rng.randrange(8,14); nmax = rng.randrange(2,5); nmin = rng.randrange(0,3)'; signdef2.log 'random stopping SSGs tested 1009, sign-definite 445 / longest all-switches run inside the class: 3'. frontier.tex l.4013-4015 ('a Max vertex over a variable and a constant switching at most twice along any improving run (lem:switch)') and l.5799 ('a vertex with one constant option flips at most twice (lem:switch)'); the bar is frontier.tex l.3228-3255 (prop:modulator-family).

findings.defect: The reported numbers contradict the route's own logs, in the direction that flatters its own family, and the discarded data contains two records the route did not claim. Report: 'the two-lane version gives 8,11,13,13,15 at m = 5,7,8,9,11'. Logs: lanes_3_4 best 12 at m=7 (reported 11), lanes_4_5 best 14 at m=9 (reported 13), lanes_4_7 best 16 at m=11 (not reported at all). I re-verified all six saved lane normal forms in exact rational arithmetic (every float is dyadic) and then BUILT two of them as raw one-player stopping SSGs through the dyadic interval-tree of lem:dyadic-row: lanes_4_5 -> N = 1675, 9 Max, stopping, 0 ties over all 512 strategies, acyclic USO, max BA height 14; lanes_4_7 -> N = 2015, 11 Max, stopping, 0 ties over all 2048 strategies, acyclic USO, max BA height 16. Hence h*_1(9) >= 14 and h*_1(11) >= 16 (and, by prop:oneplayer-lp, h*_LP and h*_HK likewise) — both new, both further than the route's own oph:h78 reaches, both obtained from a two-line lane family with ONE state per row rather than from annealing or from oph:stack. The route threw them away as a failure.
findings.evidence: /tmp/.../one-player-howard/lanes_3_4.log 'best 12', lanes_4_5.log 'best 14', lanes_4_7.log 'best 16'; auditor files /tmp/.../audit-oph/L45_GAME.json (N=1675, maxBA 14) and L47_GAME.json (N=2015, maxBA 16), built by build_lane.py and checked by reduce.py/ver.py.

findings.defect: 'a NONDEGENERATE one-player stopping SSG with 7k Max vertices ... for every k' is not proved and not verified beyond k = 2. oph:stack's proof pins the sign of C_b only in two regimes (copy j at sigma^0 with x_{v_{j-1}} <= x^-_j, and x_{v_{j-1}} = x^+_j); it says nothing at strategies where copy j has left sigma^0 while copy j-1 is still running, so ties there are not excluded. t_stack2.py checks only the run from the designated start, never the 2^{7k} incidences. I checked nondegeneracy exhaustively at k = 1 (128 strategies, 0 ties) and k = 2 (16384 strategies, 0 ties, acyclic, max BA height exactly 24); for k >= 3 it is unverified. Since h*_1, h*_LP and h*_HK are defined on nondegenerate games (rem:four-ceilings, def:improvement-uso), the claim h*_1(7k) >= 12k for k >= 3 is not established as stated. What IS established for all k is the run length 12k, which by cor:ceiling-general gives only h*(7k) >= 12k — far below thm:blowup's 2^{m/2+1}-2 and therefore worthless.
findings.evidence: t_stack2.py asserts only 'len(sets) == 12*j' and pointwise monotonicity; oph:stack's proof text has exactly two cases, 'Freezing' and 'Running'. Auditor check: ST1 m=7 ties=0 USO acyclic HK maxBA 12; ST2 m=14 ties=0 acyclic maxBA 24 (116 s, exact).

findings.defect: Vacuous. 'h*_1(7) >= 12 is attained by an explicit 7-Max-vertex game (ST(1)), not merely by monotonicity in m' — the paper's monotonicity clause is itself a construction of an explicit nondegenerate 7-Max game: 'h*_1 is nondecreasing (adjoin a Max vertex over t_0 and a fresh coin of intermediate value that no other vertex sees)', with the nondegeneracy noted explicitly at rem:four-ceilings. So the m=6 record plus one adjoined vertex already IS the explicit 7-Max game, on 348 vertices rather than ST(1)'s 734. The second clause (h*_1(8) >= 13) is real and I confirmed it exactly and then built the game myself (N = 2691) since the route never built one.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.6572-6574 and l.6603-6606; auditor's nfver.py on record_m8_L13.json: ties 0, USO, acyclic, Holt-Klee, max BA height 13, run from sigma=25 exactly as claimed; build_m8.py -> M8_GAME.json (N=2691, 8 Max, 2681 avg), run recomputed from the raw graph = 13.

findings.defect: The proof's error term is short by a factor 1/(1-rho). It says 'the pad contributes pi_{b,c} x_omega <= varsigma/(1-rho) to an action value, so it perturbs each comparison by at most varsigma/(1-rho)'. The pad is injected at every state and propagates through (I-P0_sigma)^{-1}, whose row sums are 1/(1-rho0) = 4096 on the m=6 block, so the true bound is ~2 rho varsigma/(1-rho)^2 and the stated hypothesis varsigma < (1-rho) mu g_min/2 does not imply the conclusion. The built family is safe by a huge margin (varsigma = vars_j ~ 2^-60 mu g_min, corrected requirement ~2^-24 mu g_min), and the oph:stack proof itself uses the correct argument (exact annihilation of the constant vector by (p^{b,1}-p^{b,0}).1 = 0), so this is a repair to the lemma's proof, not to the family.

The claim is TRUE — I reproduced it — but the archived evidence covers only half the cases it asserts. The route's per-split table names n=5 (m=1,2,3,4) and n=6 (m=2,3,4,5), yet the only completed logs are exh_5_1 (n=5,m=1), exh_6_3, exh_6_4 and exh1_m5; exh_6_2.err stops at 'new best 2' with no 'done' line, and there is no log at all for n=5 with m=2,3,4. Reproduced here with my own build of exh.c: n=5 m=1..5 all give L = m; n=6 m=2 (481890304 games, 183985794 stopping) gives L = 2; n=6 m=5 gives L = 5 (an independent cross-check of exh1.c); n=6 m=6 gives L = 6. The census stands.
findings.evidence: /tmp/.../one-player-howard/exh_6_2.err (truncated); auditor runs in /tmp/.../audit-oph/e62.err 'n=6 m=2 a=4 done: 481890304 games 183985794 stopping best L=2', e65.err 'best L=5', e66.err 'best L=6', plus foreground n=5 m=2,3,4,5 all L=m.

findings.defect: Float-only, and the claim is unsupported by the project's own standing rule. netv.py evaluates with numpy floats and 'if np.any(np.abs(d) < eps) and not allow_ties: return -1', so every family with a near-tie is silently discarded rather than measured; nothing was re-checked exactly. The accompanying reasoning misattributes: 'a wave whose switched sets are singletons is forbidden (cor:isolated)' — cor:isolated says a vertex that switches alone never switches again; the bound on a block of singleton rounds is prop:serialiser. And the symmetry argument does not cover the scanned families, four of whose five boundary conventions break the cyclic symmetry it invokes. This is a hand-picked negative search over 32040 shapes nobody proposed; it should not be a numbered result.
findings.evidence: netv.py score(): numpy np.linalg.solve, eps=1e-9, the tie-discard line; shapes.log: 'evaluated 32040 families; superlinear-looking: 0'. frontier.tex l.4152-4160 (cor:isolated), l.7296-7307 (prop:serialiser).

findings.defect: No comparison with lem:hstar-super, the paper's existing superadditivity lemma (h*(k+l) >= h*(k)+h*(l), by a conditional translation that runs both blocks at once), and no attribution of the mechanism. This omission actually costs the route its strongest defence: rem:four-ceilings records that lem:hstar-super's products FAIL Holt-Klee at block dimensions (4,4),(4,5),(5,4),(5,5), so by prop:oneplayer-lp they are not one-player realisable — which is exactly why oph:stack is needed and is exactly what makes it new. Attribution: the freezing bias released when a monotonically rising value crosses a threshold is the standard clock/gate of the policy-iteration lower-bound literature (Friedmann on parity games, Fearnley on MDPs — from memory, unchecked against the sources); the route flags this only obliquely in next_steps and not in the LaTeX.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.5166-5215 (lem:hstar-super) and l.6597-6603 (the products' Holt-Klee failures); the route's LaTeX for oph:stack cites neither.

findings.defect: The route frames a cap as progress. oph:stack makes h*_1 superadditive up to one state, so by Fekete's lemma lim_m h*_1(m)/m EXISTS and equals sup_{m_0} h*_1(m_0)/(m_0+1). That upgrades limsup to lim (a real gain) but it also PROVES that no amount of composition can ever produce superlinearity: the slope of every stacked family is capped by the best single block, so 'the scheduling half of a superlinear construction is solved' is more honestly read as 'the scheduling half is now known to be useless for the target'. It also makes the route's own equivalence claim redundant: 'by oph:stack that single statement is equivalent to h*_1(m) = omega(m)' is a tautology in both directions without oph:stack. And note the family's slope 12/7 = 1.714 is BELOW the ratio at the best known isolated points (h*_1(5) >= 10 and h*_1(6) >= 12 both give 2); what the family buys is that a ratio > 1 persists for all m, at the price of dropping the ratio from 2 to 12/7.
findings.evidence: oph:family gives h*_1(m_1+k(m_0+1)) >= h_1 + k h_0; oph:h5 gives h*_1(5) >= 10 (ratio 2) and prop:oneplayer-runs gives h*_1(6) >= 12 (ratio 2).

findings.result_name: unclaimed gain: h*_HK and h*_LP grow linearly
findings.defect: The route's own family yields a fact about Holt-Klee AUSOs it does not state. ST(k) is a nondegenerate one-player stopping game, so by prop:oneplayer-lp its improvement orientation is an LP orientation and hence Holt-Klee; therefore h*_HK(7k) >= 12k and h*_LP(7k) >= 12k. Before this, rem:four-ceilings had only h*_HK(m) >= 13 for all m >= 7 — a CONSTANT. This is the first linear lower bound on the Holt-Klee ceiling, and it is precisely the doubling that rem:four-ceilings says lem:hstar-super fails to deliver ('so lem:hstar-super preserves Holt-Klee for some pairs of factors and not others and no doubling follows'). Verified: ST1's orientation is Holt-Klee of height 12 at m=7 (my own max-flow test, validated by correctly rejecting B^2 on the 3-face (0,1,3)); ST2 is nondegenerate with height 24 at m=14, hence Holt-Klee by prop:oneplayer-lp.
findings.evidence: auditor nf_from_game.py on ST1_GAME.json: 'm= 7 ties= 0 USO= True acyclic= True max BA height= 12 / Holt-Klee: True'; hk.py on the paper's B^2 outmap returns (False, ((0,1,3), 16, 2, 3)) as prop:b2-realised requires.

findings.defect: The route's proposed sub-goal is provably impossible at the sizes it annealed, and it missed the cheap version of the same idea. Clause (a) asks for a balanced form on m states with run >= 2(m+1); at m <= 5 that is impossible, since a one-player run is at most h*_1(m) <= h*_LP(m) <= h*_HK(m) and h*_HK(5) = 11 < 12 (prop:hkfive, PROVED exhaustively), h*_1(4) = 6 < 10, h*_1(3) = 4 < 8. The route did not notice. What it should have asked instead is the +1-free version: oph:stack's slope is h_0/(m_0+1) only because balancing costs a fresh state omega; a block that is BALANCED BY CONSTRUCTION (all 2m_0 rows of equal state mass) gives slope h_0/m_0 outright, so a balanced 6-state form of height 12, or a balanced 5-state form of height 10 (its own oph:h5 game has height 10 but masses [4075,4029],[4095,4070],[3107,4088],[2062,4094],[3801,3571],[4074,3078]), would raise the slope from 12/7 to 2 with no new record at all. Padding onto an existing state cannot balance a block unless it has a state of value below g_min/|Delta mass| ~ 2.8e-5, and the m=6 block's values are all near 0.82 — so the question is whether the balance constraint costs height, and that is one annealing run away.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.6040 (prop:hkfive, h*_HK(5) = 11), l.6020 (cor:hstar-one, h*_1(4) = 6); blockdata.py MASS and g_min = 1.430e-05, g_max = 0.0651.

findings.defect: Fully confirmed and worth having, but it is a free read-off, not new mathematics: def:subcube and lem:subgame (both already in the paper) say the facet orientation of a one-player game is realised by a one-player game, and the height-10 facet was sitting inside round 15's own m=6 record. I recomputed all twelve facets of B6_GAME's orientation independently: heights 6,6,6,6,6,7,6,8,10,6,8,5, every one an acyclic Holt-Klee USO — matching the route's list exactly, with the 10 at (coordinate 4, value 0). Independently confirmed from the raw 346-vertex game: 5 Max, stopping, 0 ties over all 32 strategies, acyclic USO, Holt-Klee, max BA height 10, run 10 from start 10 with the stated switched sets. So h*_1(5) >= 10 and h*_LP(5) >= 10 stand and rem:four-ceilings' '>= 9' entries were already stale when they were written.

verdict:
INTEGRATE, BUT AT ABOUT A THIRD OF THE SUBMITTED LENGTH. Nothing in the report is false — I re-verified every numerical claim independently, in exact rational arithmetic, from my own code, and built two games the route never built. The paper gets better, but only if the redundant half is cut.

WORTH INTEGRATING. (1) oph:stack + oph:family, as the one genuinely new theorem: a freezing bias sequences k copies of a block at a cost of one dead state and ZERO rounds per copy, so h*_1 is superadditive up to one state. This is not covered by cor:gate/thm:zero-timer, whose bound T <= m - m_r forces a zero-tie chain of k blocks to obey k h_0 <= (k-1)m_0 + h_0, impossible for the m=6 block since h_0 = 12 > 6 = m_0; the copies here are alive throughout, so thm:zero-timer simply does not apply. It must be stated ALONGSIDE lem:hstar-super, whose abstract product achieves the same addition but leaves the Holt-Klee class at the interesting block dimensions and is therefore not one-player realisable — that contrast is the result's whole point and the route omits it. Add the two corollaries the route missed: Fekete (lim h*_1(m)/m = sup_{m_0} h*_1(m_0)/(m_0+1), hence composition is CAPPED by the best block and can never be superlinear — state this as the negative it is) and h*_HK(7k) >= 12k, h*_LP(7k) >= 12k, the first linear lower bound on the Holt-Klee ceiling. (2) oph:h5, as a repair to rem:four-ceilings (h*_1(5), h*_LP(5) become >= 10). (3) The table extension, but the RIGHT one: h*_1(8) >= 13 from the annealed record (I built the game, N = 2691), and h*_1(9) >= 14, h*_1(11) >= 16 from the route's own DISCARDED lane data (I built both games, N = 1675 and N = 2015, both stopping, nondegenerate, acyclic USO). The one-player row should read 1, 2, 4, 6, >=10, >=12, >=12, >=13, >=14, ?, >=16 for m = 1..11, plus h*_1(7k) >= 12k. (4) oph:exhaustive, as one sentence inside rem:grid-per-vertex: at n <= 6 the truth is the stronger L <= |Vmax|, so the smallest one-player game with L > |Vmax| has at least 7 non-sink vertices. I reproduced the four (n,m) cases whose logs were missing or truncated.

NOT WORTH INTEGRATING AS WRITTEN. oph:dictionary and rem:oph:v3 — cut to one remark: 'claim (v3) is lem:readout at k=0 together with thm:readout-realise(b) at r=1, and is thereby settled in both directions', with a pointer to lem:rise-bound for the collapse identity. A full proposition with a fresh two-direction proof is a rediscovery of the paper's own round-15 section and would be the twenty-first such case on the list. oph:signdef — keep ONLY rem:signdef-scope's contrapositive as a labelled design lemma ('a run longer than 2|Vmax| needs a Max vertex whose two first-passage laws differ in sign on C'), cite the paper's two existing prose statements of its m=1 case, and DELETE the polynomial-class claim until a member outside the eight is exhibited to prop:modulator-family's standard; as it stands the class has no separating witness and every sampled instance is in the trivial min(m,k) = O(log N) class. oph:h78's first clause — delete, it is what rem:four-ceilings' monotonicity clause already constructs. oph:negative — delete both halves: (i) is a float screen that discards near-ties, and (ii)'s numbers contradict its own logs and its discarded winners are two of the new records above.

THE TRUE REMAINING GAP, sharper than the route states it: the route says 'a sequence of one-player games with h_t/m_t -> infinity', which is the target restated. What oph:stack actually leaves is this — EXHIBIT ONE NONDEGENERATE ONE-PLAYER STOPPING SSG WITH ALL 2m ROWS OF EQUAL STATE MASS WHOSE ALL-SWITCHES RUN EXCEEDS 2m; equivalently, since oph:stack makes lim h*_1(m)/m = sup_{m_0} h*_1(m_0)/(m_0+1), the entire question is now whether that supremum is finite, and the first obstruction is not the construction but the ceiling h*_HK, which is PROVED equal to 11 at m = 5 and known only to be >= 12, >= 13 at m = 6, 7. No scheduling, stacking or alarm construction can touch this, by oph:stack itself; the cheapest decisive experiment is to re-run the m = 5 and m = 6 anneals with the balance constraint imposed (a balanced 6-state block of height 12, or a balanced 5-state block of height 10, doubles the family's slope from 12/7 to 2 with no new record), and after that to decide h*_HK(7) >= 14, where 12 is what oph:family gives and 16 is what the quadratic law would predict.
